subject: Dictation quality: measured A/B over a labelled Italian corpus
request: Improve dictation, keep the previous pipeline as a benchmark, vary male and female voices and noise conditions.

corpus.source: PolyAI/minds14, config it-IT, via the public HuggingFace datasets API. Real Italian speech with human reference transcripts.
corpus.voices: 7 male (median F0 96-105 Hz) and 7 female (182-190 Hz). Gender is not labelled in the dataset, so it is estimated by autocorrelation F0 and recorded per clip.
conditions: wind-15 and wind-5: brown noise with slow gusts, the wind a boat crew records into
babble-10: overlapping speech from other clips
corpus.note: The audio is 8 kHz G.711 mu-law telephone speech, which makes absolute error rates high. Only the relative comparison is meaningful. The corpus is built outside the repository and is never committed.

harnessDefect: The first corpus was silently corrupt: the source files are WAV format tag 7 (mu-law) and the reader decoded them as linear PCM. Every early number was measured on distorted audio and was discarded. The reader now handles mu-law and A-law.

results.metric: word error rate, percent, lower is better; LOOP is the share of clips whose output exceeded three times the reference length

findings: The dominant failure was not mishearing but repetition collapse. One six-word reference produced a 444-word output. Generation brakes (no_repeat_ngram_size 5, repetition_penalty 1.15, temperature 0, condition_on_previous_text false) removed every loop and took aggregate error from 303% to 90%.
Classic DSP did not help. A chain of DC removal, an 80 Hz high pass, RMS normalisation and silence trimming measured 90.5% against 89.9% without it, which is inside the noise. It was not shipped.
The model is the remaining lever. whisper-base under the same guard roughly halved the error rate against whisper-tiny, for 73 MB of first-use download instead of 39 MB.
Male and female voices improved by the same margin at every stage, so a per-voice model or per-voice DSP is not justified.
shipped: TRANSCRIPTION_GUARD applied to every request in src/capabilities/speech.ts
reproduce: npm run speech:bench -- <corpus> [url] [variants], against a corpus built by fetch-balanced.mjs then build-corpus.mjs. The harness moved from this directory to scripts/speech-bench/ on 2026-09-21 and is documented in its README; variants.js still holds every pipeline tried, including the original as 'baseline', so the comparison can be repeated.
notVerified: No physical microphone pass. Chromium's fake audio capture did not inject the file in this environment, so end-to-end dictation was exercised with a real recording only through the benchmark, not through the microphone.
